fields.statement: Verifier at b7cf6e6c. Read the diff: buildRetire drops the change set's own pending update/move ops and writes the retire on the landed version; staleRetire now counts a retire as stale when the change set also holds its own update or move on the node, which fixes attempt 1's finding f1. Tests: TestRetire/SupersedesPendingEdits (handle+move+retire leaves one retire on the landed base), SupersedesPendingEditsLands (lands, folds clean), and RepairsStaleRetire / RepairsStaleRetireAfterMove / RepairsRetireOnUpdate build the old shape (update [+move] and retire all on the landed base), repair it with retire, and land it (covers f2). go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestRetire|TestStackedWrites' passed; go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'Retire|Write|Land|Fold|Stacked|Set|Mv|Move' passed every test (afterwards the package's harness flagged only the known .rhiza-root/usage.live.json leak from the enclosing ~/code root, unrelated to this leaf); go test -trimpath ./internal/model/... ok; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/retire-after-update ok. The whole internal/api package needs longer than go test's default 10m (the Makefile uses 20m), so I scoped the run. By hand, in scratch repos with RHIZA_* unset: the pre-fix binary (4b2082fa) wrote set --handle (and in a second repo, mv) then retire, all on the landed base, and its land exited 3; then the new binary's retire <node-id> exited 0, left one node.retire on the landed base, and land exited 0, in both repos.
